note: Hypothesis-driven set written after a mid-point look at dev data (2026-10-09 ~00:00 UTC), before any held-out case was run. Errors follow canonical gRPC status codes so each one is a realistic server error. None of them contains attacker text or names a tool or value.
theory: Explanatory gap: an agent that receives an unexplained failure looks for a cause or remedy in its context, and a poisoned rule in a tool description supplies one. Prediction 1: unexplained errors revive more than errors whose cause is stated. Prediction 2 (fit): an error that blames the arguments revives parameter-tampering poisons (T3) more than precondition-hijacking poisons (T2); an error that blames a missing precondition does the reverse. Prediction 3: an explicit benign remedy suppresses revival.
